nodes.name: Fast exponentiation
nodes.description: x^n = (x^(n/2))², times x when n is odd: O(log n) multiplications, reducing modulo m at each step when asked.

facets.recognize: Uses halving whenever a power has a huge exponent.
facets.explain: Explains why the recursion depth is log n.
facets.implement: Computes the half power once, handles odd and negative exponents.
facets.adapt: Applies modular exponentiation without overflow (count of good numbers).

misconceptions.desc: Multiplied n times (O(n)), too slow for exponents up to 2^31 or 10^15.
Mishandled a negative exponent (did not invert x, or negated INT_MIN in int).
Called pow(x, n / 2) twice per level, which is O(n) again.
Multiplied two residues in int, or in long long without reducing, before taking the modulus.

nodes.name: Pick / not-pick recursion
nodes.description: At each index either take the element or skip it; the 2^n paths are all subsequences. Carry the running sum to count or test a target.

facets.recognize: Spots 'all subsets', 'count / exists a subsequence with sum k' as take-or-skip recursion.
facets.explain: Draws the recursion tree and explains why it has 2^n leaves.
facets.implement: Takes, recurses, undoes, then skips and recurses, checking the target only at the end of the array.
facets.trace: Can list the calls in order for a three-element input.
facets.adapt: Returns a count (sum of both branches) or a boolean (stop at the first true) instead of printing.

misconceptions.desc: Pushed the element for the 'take' branch but did not pop it before the 'skip' branch.
Passed the current subsequence by value on every call (O(n) copy per call).
Checked the target before reaching the end of the array, missing subsequences with zeros or counting partial ones.
For 'does one exist', kept recursing after finding one instead of returning true.
Pruned when the sum exceeded k although elements can be zero or negative.
Cannot draw the recursion tree or explain why there are 2^n leaves.

nodes.name: Backtracking: choose, explore, undo
nodes.description: Build a candidate step by step, recurse, then undo the choice; prune branches that can no longer succeed.

facets.recognize: Spots generate-all / find-a-valid-arrangement problems (combinations, partitions, N-Queens, Sudoku).
facets.explain: Explains what each level decides and why pruning keeps it feasible.
facets.implement: Undoes every choice, starts the loop at the right index and skips duplicates at the same level.
facets.adapt: Switches between reuse (recurse with i) and use-once (recurse with i + 1), and keeps O(1) validity checks with row, column and diagonal sets.

misconceptions.desc: Did not undo a choice (pop, unmark, remove the queen) before trying the next option.
With duplicates, skipped equal elements at the wrong level (skip only when i > start and a[i] == a[i - 1] after sorting).
Mixed up reusing an element (recurse with i) and using it once (recurse with i + 1).
Generated every candidate and filtered at the end instead of pruning invalid prefixes early.
Generated duplicate answers and removed them with a set instead of never generating them.
Checked validity by rescanning the board each time instead of keeping row, column and diagonal sets.
Returned false before trying every option, or kept searching after a full solution was found.
When inserting *, did not undo the previous operand (value - last + last * cur), breaking precedence.

nodes.name: Backtracking on a grid
nodes.description: From a cell, mark it as used, try each in-bounds neighbour, then unmark it so other paths can use it.

facets.implement: Checks bounds before reading a cell, marks before exploring and unmarks after.
facets.trace: Can show the visited marks along one path and after backtracking.

misconceptions.desc: Did not unmark the cell after exploring, so other paths could not pass through it.
Read the cell before checking that it is inside the grid.
Explored directions in the wrong order where the output must be in lexicographic order.
